sub_graphs.title: EIP-211: Return Data Buffer Lifecycle
sub_graphs.description: Models the lifecycle of the return data buffer across call frames, including clearing, population, and access

nodes.label: Call Frame Active
nodes.description: EVM is executing within an active call frame with its own return data buffer

nodes.label: Return Data Buffer Empty
nodes.description: Return data buffer has been cleared, size is zero

nodes.label: Return Data Buffer Populated
nodes.description: Return data buffer contains data from a completed call, size reflects actual data length

nodes.label: Clear Return Data Buffer
nodes.description: Clear the return data buffer before executing a call-like opcode (CALL, DELEGATECALL, CREATE, etc.)

nodes.label: Execute Call-Like Opcode
nodes.description: Execute CALL, DELEGATECALL, CALLCODE, STATICCALL, CREATE, or CREATE2 opcode

nodes.label: Populate Return Data Buffer
nodes.description: Store complete return data (or failure data) from the call into the caller's return data buffer

nodes.label: Subcall Completed
nodes.description: The called contract has finished execution (success or failure), return data available

edges.label: Call-like opcode encountered, initiate buffer clear

sub_graphs.title: EIP-211: RETURNDATASIZE and RETURNDATACOPY Execution
sub_graphs.description: Models the runtime execution of RETURNDATASIZE (0x3d) and RETURNDATACOPY (0x3e) opcodes

nodes.label: RETURNDATASIZE Opcode Fetched
nodes.description: EVM has fetched opcode 0x3d (RETURNDATASIZE) for execution

nodes.label: Read Return Data Buffer Size
nodes.description: Read the current size of the return data buffer

nodes.label: Push Size to Stack
nodes.description: Push the return data buffer size value onto the EVM stack

nodes.label: Size Value on Stack
nodes.description: Return data buffer size has been pushed to stack, opcode complete

nodes.label: RETURNDATACOPY Opcode Fetched
nodes.description: EVM has fetched opcode 0x3e (RETURNDATACOPY) for execution

nodes.label: Pop Copy Parameters
nodes.description: Pop destOffset, offset, and length from stack for RETURNDATACOPY

nodes.label: Validate Buffer Bounds
nodes.description: Check if offset + length <= RETURNDATASIZE and no overflow

nodes.label: Bounds Check Passed
nodes.description: The requested range is within the return data buffer bounds

nodes.label: Bounds Check Failed
nodes.description: Requested range exceeds return data buffer or overflow detected

nodes.label: Copy Data to Memory
nodes.description: Copy bytes from return data buffer to EVM memory at destOffset

nodes.label: Data Copied to Memory
nodes.description: Return data has been successfully copied to memory

nodes.label: Trigger Out-of-Gas Exception
nodes.description: Halt execution with out-of-gas exception due to bounds violation

nodes.label: Execution Halted (OOG)
nodes.description: Current call has stopped due to out-of-gas exception

sub_graphs.title: EIP-211: Return Data Operations Gas Costs
sub_graphs.description: Models the gas consumption for RETURNDATASIZE and RETURNDATACOPY operations

nodes.label: Gas Available for Execution
nodes.description: Current call frame has gas available for opcode execution

nodes.label: Charge RETURNDATASIZE Gas
nodes.description: Deduct 2 gas for RETURNDATASIZE opcode (same as CALLDATASIZE)

nodes.label: Compute RETURNDATACOPY Gas
nodes.description: Calculate gas: 3 + 3 * ceil(length / 32) for memory copy

nodes.label: Charge RETURNDATACOPY Gas
nodes.description: Deduct computed gas for RETURNDATACOPY operation

nodes.label: Gas Successfully Deducted
nodes.description: Required gas has been deducted, operation can proceed

nodes.label: Insufficient Gas
nodes.description: Not enough gas available, operation cannot proceed

ambiguities.text: The specification states reading zero bytes from the buffer's end succeeds, but the exact boundary condition semantics are implicit
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume offset == RETURNDATASIZE with length == 0 is valid (empty read at end). This allows contracts to safely probe buffer boundaries.

ambiguities.text: The specification does not explicitly state what happens to the return data buffer when a call fails vs succeeds
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume failure data (revert reason) is stored in the same buffer as success data. The caller must check the call's success status separately.

implicit_assumptions.description: The return data buffer is isolated per call frame and cannot be accessed across different execution contexts
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Cross-frame return data access could leak sensitive information between unrelated contract calls

implicit_assumptions.description: The called contract cannot manipulate the caller's return data buffer except through normal return mechanisms
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Malicious contracts could corrupt the caller's view of return data, leading to incorrect contract logic

implicit_assumptions.description: An attacker controlling a called contract can return arbitrary data, but this data is properly bounded and validated by RETURNDATACOPY
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Buffer overflow vulnerabilities could allow memory corruption in the calling contract
